newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish T-bill yields seen flat at primary tender.
newsitem.headline: Polish T-bill yields seen flat at primary tender.

text.p: Polish T-bill yields are likely to hold flat at Thursday's 400 million zloty primary tender, because the finance ministry did not need cash and was unlikely to agree to a yield rise, dealers said.

They said the aim of the additional Thursday tender was to stabilise yields at present levels rather than raise funds as the treasury's liquidity needs were likely to be already satisfied in December.
"The treasury has probably large funds coming from the public sale of one-year and three-year bonds, it will not allow prices to fall," said Piotr Korcz from Bank Handlowy SA. @
Analysts said secondary market yields were on the rise because of recent central bank statements that it was mulling a near-term rise in nominal interest rates to stop fast credit growth.

Analysts said demand should not top 600 million zlotys with corporate focus on 13-week T-bills which were quoted above the 19.00 percent on the secondary market against the average yield of 18.77 percent on the last primary tender.
Banks were expected to focus demand on the longest 52-week T-bills, which were at 19.60 percent on the secondary market against the average 19.57 percent on the last primary tender. @
Small interest was expected on the half-year paper, which were at 19.30 percent in secondary trade against the average primary yield of 19.25 percent.
Analysts did not expect any foreign entry because of the record strangth of the zloty which firmed to 3.20 percent from the trdaing band centre on Wednesday.
